labels.notes: Checked against BTZ_1.tex l.1274-1279 and OQ-152 (a) (OPEN). common_reg_of_isometry (CommonRegIso.lean:152) keeps every printed hypothesis (globally hyperbolic, IsE0CauchyMaximal, E0CauchyCompact, for both M and N). It reads « reg(M) ≃ reg(N) » as f : e0RegMFlat M → e0RegMFlat N with Causal.Flat.IsIsometricEmbedding 2 f and Surjective f. That is a bijective local isometry, so an isometry of the flat spacetimes. The conclusion is a homeomorphism that is an E0-morphism both ways and extends f, which is stronger than the printed M ≃ N. IsIsometricEmbedding (lean-causal/Causal/Flat/FlatSpacetime.lean:312) is the real notion and is not vacuous: continuity, plus at every point the chart reading agrees near x with the action of an element of isom d = SO0(1,d) ⋉ R^{d+1} (Form.lean:132,198), plus injectivity. The isometries in this reading preserve orientation and time orientation. That is the structure group of the E0 category, the same group the E0-morphism reading uses, so it is not a narrowing. common_reg_either takes the disjunction of the two readings (it is no weaker than either) and concludes F with E0-morphisms both ways. The bridge isE0Mor_of_isIsometricEmbedding (isometry ⇒ E0-morphism of the open sets e0RegM) is faithful: it goes through E0AbsMax.isE0Mor_regExt, the identity lemmas isE0Mor_flatE0Val and isE0Mor_toFlatE0 (which state that the identity Reg N → N and Reg N → FlatE0 (e0RegMFlat N) are E0-morphisms), and isE0Mor_corestrict_iff. regMap is just the carrier identity (e0RegMFlat_carrier is rfl). Added hypothesis: M and N connected. It is inherited from common_reg (OQ-150 (b), DEC-125 (e)), e0RegMFlat needs it, and it is disclosed as ⚠ strengthened. The docstring has no ** mark. The E0-only scope (T-btz-scope) and OQ-152 are disclosed in SCOPE and left open: the closer took no decision. The curation row stays lean_proved_override = "partial" and was not edited.
